one_month_reasoning: There is no Synopsys print in the window. Q4 FY26 results come in early December, and the FY27 guide was given at the 2026-09-30 Investor Day [2]. Three scheduled events fall inside it. (1) Cadence Q3 results, estimated 2026-10-26 (unconfirmed) [15,24], are the main read-across on EDA demand and AI-agent monetisation. (2) The FOMC meets on Oct 27-28 [18]. The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% in September and 16 of 18 members expect at least one more hike in 2026 [18]. A hike is therefore largely expected, but a hawkish surprise would weigh on long-duration software multiples. (3) The ~$1B buyback is executing 'over the coming months' [2], a mild support. Post-guidance drift argues up: the FY27 EPS guide of $19.08 beat consensus by ~7% [2,13], and brokers raised targets [23]. Reversal risk argues down after a +33% run in 2.5 weeks ($367.70 to $490.54 [14]). I treat these as roughly offsetting. So the median stays at spot (P(>=490.54)=0.50) with log-sigma 13.5%, slightly above the usual annual vol / 3.5 = 12.9% because two macro and peer events sit in the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods on FY28 numbers, as of Oct 2027. FY28 EPS $22.9 (FY27 guide $19.08 x 1.20) x 24x = $550 (50%). FY28 FCF $3.78B at a 3.7% equity yield over 190M shares = $538 (30%). FY28 non-GAAP EBITDA ~$6.1B x 17x, less ~$5.0B net debt, over 190M shares = $520 (20%). Blended: ~$540. Multiples were trimmed for the September Fed hike, and the EV/EBITDA multiple is now anchored to primary-derived current multiples, not a Substack.

inputs_detail.derivation: The company's FY26-30 mid-20s EPS CAGR from $15.07 implies ~23%/yr after FY27 [2], and BofA computes 23% [23]. I haircut to 20% because Amazon/AWS licensing timing is undisclosed [2,11] and because of China (~10% of revenue [22]) and IP-credibility risk.

Today the stock trades at 25.7x the FY27 guide (490.54/19.08 [2,14]) and was ~19x at the September low. I trimmed my exit multiple from 25x to 24x after the Fed's September hike and a dot plot with no cuts in 2027 [18]. Cadence trades at a much higher forward multiple, but the AI-disruption overhang [7,16] justifies holding SNPS below its own history.

The current yield on FY27 FCF is 3.1B/(490.54 x 192.3M) = 3.3% [1,2]. I use 3.7%, up from 3.6% in round 1, for de-rating risk under a hiking Fed [18]. This is not SBC-burdened: SBC is ~$970M [2], so this method leans optimistic, and that is part of why it does not carry the most weight.

Rebuilt from primary data rather than the discounted Substack multiple. Current EV is ~$100.7B (490.54 x 192.3M + $6.4B net debt [1,14]); valueinvesting.io shows $101.6B [19]. That is ~19.5x FY27 non-GAAP EBITDA of ~$5.16B (11.15 x 44% + 0.25 [2]), and was ~15x at the September low. The 41.5x GAAP trailing figure [19] is distorted by Ansys deal costs and is not comparable. I use 17x one year forward, below today's 19.5x, for the rate path [18].
Today $10.04B debt less $3.61B cash = $6.4B (10-Q [22], 8-K [1]). Add Q4 FY26 plus FY27 FCF of ~$3.8B and subtract ~$1.5B+ of buybacks [2]. Result: ~$4.8-5.0B.

bear.story: Rates keep rising (one more 2026 hike, no 2027 cuts [18]) and the AI-disruption narrative returns. A Kimi-K3-style demo knocked 7.85% off SNPS in one day [16,17], and practitioners flag AI-native verification startups [5]. China export-control risk returns (~10% of revenue [22]), and the class action (response due 2026-11-04 [22]) keeps IP credibility in focus. The multiple compresses to ~17-18x on a trimmed FY28 EPS of ~$19-20.

base.story: Synopsys delivers the FY27 guide ($11.15B, $19.08 [2]). The market pays ~24x FY28 EPS of ~$22-23, a slight de-rating from today's 25.7x forward given the rate path [18]. AgentEngineer reaches general availability by end-2026 with 50+ customer engagements [20,21], Ansys synergies and buybacks support EPS, and AWS/OpenAI licensing shows up gradually [2].

bull.story: Agentic AI raises tool consumption, as Cadence's CEO argues [6], and consumption-based pricing for Autopilot/AgentEngineer [20] gains traction. The AWS licensing deal [2] lands early, and FY28 EPS of ~$23.5+ earns ~30x even with higher rates. That is about the HSBC $700 target [13]. The Monte Investments $710 figure [3] is narrative only, not an input.

thesis_break_reason: $350 sits below the 52-week low ($362.55 intraday / $367.70 close [14]) and at ~18.3x the FY27 EPS guide [2], so a close there would mean the market rejects the guidance given on 9/30. That would most likely reflect something fundamental: a Design IP miss or FY27 cut at the December print, renewed China EDA restrictions, or a credible AI/open-source share-loss story [5,7,16]. I moved up from $340 toward the supervisor's $365, but not all the way. At 45% realised vol, a hiking Fed [18] plus a give-back of the Investor Day gap could take the stock to ~$365 with no fundamental damage. The pre-event low was itself set by sentiment shocks (Kimi -7.85% [17]), not by a guidance cut.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's established facts are now inputs. (a) The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% in September 2026 with dots at 4.1% for end-2026 and end-2027. I verified this on Chase's summary [18]; CNBC returned 403. I had cited recession odds but not the rate path, so I cut the P/E exit multiple from 25x to 24x and raised the FCF yield from 3.6% to 3.7%. (b) My EV/EBITDA leg rested on a single Substack's 16.3x/20.5x. I rebuilt it from primary data: today's EV of ~$100.7B (cross-checked at $101.6B on valueinvesting.io [19]) is ~19.5x FY27 guided non-GAAP EBITDA. I kept 17x forward but cut the leg's weight to 20%. (c) The Kimi K3 effect now rests on Seeking Alpha/Investing.com (BNP: buy the dip) and a second report of -7.85% to $384.28 [16,17], not the forum alone. (d) Substack and blog numbers (Monte $710, LYCa22, tech-insider) are narrative only. The bull case is anchored to HSBC's $700 [13] and the AWS deal to the company's own release [2]. (e) Net debt is $6.4B (10-Q [22]), China is 9.9% of revenue and the class-action response is due Nov 4 [22], all as verified by the supervisor. Blended fair value: $540 (P/E $550 x 0.5, FCF $538 x 0.3, EV/EBITDA $520 x 0.2). It matches the supervisor's figure, but I reached it independently from my own legs. Scenarios are $340/$540/$700 at 25/50/25, a mean of ~$530. For the 12-month ladder I blended 50/50 the scenario mixture (within-scenario sigmas 25/18/20%) with a lognormal at median $512 and 40% vol. The lognormal median is lower than round 1's $525 because of the rate path. Result: P(>=spot) = 0.57 (was 0.595), median ~$515. The left tail stays fat: there have been three 30%+ drawdowns since mid-2025, plus AI scares and IP credibility. In-lane alternative signals: SemiWiki practitioners dismiss Kimi but flag verification startups [5]; Cadence's CEO argues agents call more tools [6]; WARN notices show restructuring continuing [10]; 50+ AgentEngineer engagements with GA at end-2026 but pricing not finalised [20,21]. Research limits: X and Reddit block fetching, CNBC returned 403, and the round-2 verification sources are mostly outside my lane by design (filings and press used to check supervisor findings).
